Chapter 6: Making Space for “Must”—Creating Room for What Matters
Picture this—there’s this quiet moment, nothing dramatic, just a simple realization: your days are crammed with obligations, distractions, and constant noise.
The calendar’s overflowing, your phone never stops buzzing, and that to-do list? It only seems to get longer. Somewhere in all that daily chaos, the voice of “Must”—that deep, authentic calling—feels so faint, almost impossible to hear.
It’s not that your true desires are gone. They’re just... crowded out by everything else.
Imagine one evening, you’re sitting at your kitchen table, surrounded by unopened mail and projects that never quite get finished.
There’s this ache—a sense that real life is happening somewhere else, like your true self is just waiting for a chance to breathe. And suddenly, it hits you: if “Must” is ever going to have a place in your life, something else has to go.
Most of us don’t even realize how much time we spend on autopilot.
There are errands, endless emails, social events, and, let’s be honest, way too much scrolling.
The days all start to blur together, and the things that matter most? They get pushed aside.
It’s easy to tell ourselves there’s just no time for passion, no room for creativity, no space for what really feels essential.
But here’s something to pay attention to—making space for “Must” isn’t really about squeezing more hours out of your day.
It’s about making different choices.
It starts with the smallest acts of intention. Maybe you say no to just one commitment.
Or you carve out a quiet hour in the morning, or turn off your notifications for an evening.
Those little moments of stillness? That’s where your inner voice gets a chance to speak up.
For example, one person decided to keep Sunday afternoons just for painting.
At first, it felt almost selfish—like it was too much to ask for. But as the weeks went by, that weekly ritual became a lifeline.
It turned into sacred space where “Must” could finally breathe.
And by protecting that time, by treating it as non-negotiable, they were sending themselves a powerful message: this really matters.
Here’s the thing—it’s never going to be perfect.
Interruptions happen, plans fall apart, and there will be days when nothing goes as you hoped.
The key is to keep coming back, to keep making space, even if it’s just in small ways.
Over time, these choices add up, and suddenly, your life feels more spacious, more intentional, and honestly, more alive.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful small changes can be.
A few minutes of quiet, a single act of creation, a moment to reflect—these are the seeds that let “Must” grow.
It’s not a one-time thing. It’s a daily practice—a gentle, ongoing decision to choose what matters most.
